chapter: The Jelly Roll Morton records and Minton's Playhouse
title: Minton's as bebop center and reactions to the new music
summary: Minton's drew young and middle-class listeners; Dance and Caldwell say bebop was unpopular at first and not the only direction jazz could take.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Well, yeah. Well, no, the thing was when you started at Minton's, I mean it became a place where guys came to jam. Well, it wasn't only just the bebop people. I mean you had the other musicians too.

By all means. Certainly. That was the center of the bebop and the -- of course, there were a lot of places during that time too, but that was, most of it was centered (unintelligible) because they all -- like they all come up there, why don't you go get on the bandstand. I tell them they just get what you want, and they play because they know they going to get -- (unintelligible) then like they like you too.
I mean when they started doing that in Minton's, how do the people react to it?

Well, the people take to it because they -- a lot of the people was younger people and little middle class people who was fascinated with this style of jazz, so naturally they [to] hear (unintelligible) come in Dizzy and Charlie Parker because they, at that particular time, it was just getting popular because it wasn't popular at first, you know.

Well, no, I mean that's what I understand. I mean I would have thought that it at the beginning it must have sounded so ridiculous or awful that you would have thought that -- I mean the first time I heard
it, I thought it was abominable.
Well, it would to a lot of people.

I think what Fletcher said was quite right when he said that all the miseries afflict (unintelligible) bebop, is the worst, but, you know, it always seems to me that people assume that because it happened, that was the direction and the way it had to go, but --
-- it was not so because, I mean you could have had -- I mean that's not the only direction for the music to go, is it?
Definitely not, that's true, very true.
Mind you, (unintelligible). You might have had something even worse.
